primary_secondary.note: Experience-based position column; not a synthesis of studies.

research_method.claude: Conceptual essay / expert opinion based on the experience of Google's Engineering Productivity Research team; no empirical data collection
research_method.nlm: Expert opinion / position paper; inaugural 'Developer Productivity for Humans' column; conceptual, no primary dataset
research_method.value: Position paper / expert-opinion column (inaugural 'Developer Productivity for Humans' column, IEEE Software) drawing on the authors' experience leading Google's Engineering Productivity Research team; conceptual argument with no empirical data

context.claude: Industry; Google (Engineering Productivity Research team); no sample
context.value: not reported (conceptual; no empirical sample); authors' experience at Google (Engineering Productivity Research team)

space_applied.note: SPACE only cited as an example framework for selecting multiple metrics.

remote_covid.note: Hybrid/distributed teams only named as a future column topic; pandemic only as an example of external context.

data_window.note: Not stated by either (conceptual column, no data).

cat_productivity.note: Throughput metrics (lines of code per minute) discussed critically as a flawed productivity measure.

cat_quality.note: Flaky tests and technical debt appear only as productivity factors; no quality metric.

cat_collaboration.note: Code-review bias and team dispersion discussed as factors, not metrics.

cat_satisfaction.note: NotebookLM lists employee attrition/retention as a Satisfaction metric (measure of happiness); Claude classes attrition as an organizational cost and reports no satisfaction metric. Text discusses happiness and attrition in one paragraph.

cat_activity.note: Same metric (lines of code per minute), labelled Productivity (throughput) by Claude and Productivity/Activity by NotebookLM.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM labels build speed 'Delivery / DevEx'; Claude treats it as a technical factor. Build speed is discussed only as an example of a productivity factor.

cat_devex.note: Flow and context switching discussed via build speed, but the DevEx framework is not used.

cat_agile.note: Agile methods and TDD mentioned only as general best practices.

evidence.quote: The “Developer Productivity for Humans” column aims to draw attention to advances and challenges in research and practice in tools and practices that help improve developers’ day-to-day tasks.
WE LEAD A mixed-methods research team at Google that seeks to understand what makes engineers productive and happy.
We need to think about measuring productivity in a holistic and multifaceted way, not in a reductionist, unidimensional way.

Conflating throughput with productivity: One might count the lines of code written by a developer in a certain period and calculate a simple output per unit time “productivity” measure like lines of code per minute.
evidence.loc: PDF p. 3 (Software Engineering Is a Complex, Creative Endeavor)
